proposals.before: After the Six Xiu disaster, most survivors fled south with Ren Ziyun, Liu Kun's designated heir.
proposals.after: After the Six Xiu disaster, most survivors fled south with Zun, Liu Kun's designated heir.
proposals.reason: 任子遵 identifies Zun as Liu Kun’s heir-son; “Ren Ziyun” is a fused misreading.

proposals.before: Xiong styled himself Shiyuan and Dan Shiya; both were bold, resourceful men who had served as provincial aides under the Jin.
proposals.after: Xiong's style was Shiyuan, and Dan's was Shiya; both were bold, resourceful men who had served as provincial aides under the Jin.
proposals.reason: 澹字世雅 states that Shiya was Dan’s style name; the current English fuses the names.

proposals.before: Then Xiong and Dan, with Ren Ziyun, Liu Kun's heir, led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin followers into open revolt.
proposals.after: Then Xiong and Dan, with Zun, Liu Kun's heir, led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin followers into open revolt.
proposals.reason: 任子遵 names Zun; “Ren Ziyun” results from incorrect segmentation.

proposals.before: Fu Jian gave Liu Kuren's wife the surname Gongsun and loaded her with gifts.
proposals.after: Fu Jian bestowed a Gongsun woman on Liu Kuren as his wife and provided her with a rich dowry.
proposals.reason: 賜庫仁妻公孫氏 bestows a Gongsun woman as wife; it does not rename an existing wife.

proposals.before: "Outward campaigns also repelled": Northern History juan 20, this life, has dong (campaign) for xun (merit).
proposals.after: "Outward campaigns also repelled": Northern History juan 20, this life, has xun (merit) where this text has dong (campaign).
proposals.reason: Chinese 「動」作「勳」 means the Northern History reads 勳 in place of 動; the English reverses the collation direction.

proposals.before: "In outward campaigns, he also repelled": in Northern History juan 20, this biography reads dong (campaign) as xun (merit).
proposals.after: "In outward campaigns, he also repelled": in Northern History juan 20, this biography has xun (merit) for dong (campaign).
proposals.reason: Collation note 「動」作「勳」 reports the Northern History reading 勳 for this chapter's 動; the English wording is reversed.

proposals.before: Wei Cao set up a stele south of Dahang city. In Qian's Textual Notes, juan 38, we read: "This chapter preserves his inscription in full, yet the historiographers mangled the record and the authentic text was lost.
proposals.after: Wei Cao set up a stele south of Dahang city. In Qian's Textual Notes, juan 38, we read: "This biography records the stele Wei Cao erected; alas, the historiographers altered it and its original authenticity was lost.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'in full' and softens 改竄/失其本真; the Chinese does not say the inscription is preserved complete.

decisions.reason: 劉琨任子遵 is Liu Kun's heir-son Zun; Ren Ziyun fuses 任子 with 遵 into a false personal name and must be corrected.
雄字世遠，澹字世雅 assigns courtesy names separately; without a break after Shiyuan, “styled himself Shiyuan and Dan Shiya” makes both names Xiong's complement, so the clearer split attribution is required.
與劉琨任子遵 again names heir-son Zun; Ren Ziyun is the same fused misreading as in s0107 and is not supported by the Chinese.
賜庫仁妻公孫氏 means Fu Jian bestowed a Gongsun-clan woman as Kuren's wife, confirmed by later 妻兄公孫希; giving an existing wife the surname Gongsun invents a rename the Chinese does not state.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 苻堅賜庫仁妻公孫氏，厚其資送

decisions.reason: 「動」作「勳」 reports that Beishi has 勳 where this text has 動; “has dong for xun” reverses that collation direction, and the proposed wording restores it.
In collation English, “reads dong as xun” already means Beishi substitutes 勳 for this chapter's 動, matching 「動」作「勳」; the proposed rewording is stylistic clarification, not a reversal fix.
此傳載衞操所立碑 only says the biography records the stele; “preserves…in full” invents completeness, and the proposed wording better tracks 惜為史臣改竄，失其本真.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此傳載衞操所立碑……惜為史臣改竄，失其本真
